clue.text: 26 27's leader has one to tea when there's honey about — leaders contain an expression of disgust

indicators.note: the honey is said to be about, that is surrounding, the one and the tea

parts.note: mel is Latin for honey, familiar from mellifluous
the Roman numeral for one is I
cha is a slang word for tea

indicators.note: the leaders are said to hold the expression of disgust within them

parts.note: the van is the leading part of an army, its leaders
ugh is the noise of disgust

explanation.surface: A cricket captain invites someone to tea when honey is out, and his superiors put up with a grimace.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 is ENGLAND and 27 CRICKET, so the definition is England's cricket captain at the time of the puzzle; 'about' and 'contain' signal the two insertions.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Vaughan captained the England Test cricket team from 2003 to 2008.

clue.text: Partnership's taking a month and country a year off

parts.note: Mar is the short form of March

indicators.note: the year is taken off, removed from the country's name

parts.note: Italy is a country
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A couple's relationship involves a month away and a year abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals the year is dropped from the country; 'Partnership's' is the definition read as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Marital describes what belongs to a married partnership, so it fits the possessive form of the word.

clue.text: No beggar could manage the company horse

indicators.note: manage suggests handling the letters and working them into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone without money might be able to run the firm's horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could manage' rearranges CO and HORSE. The proverb 'beggars can't be choosers' makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: From the proverb that beggars can't be choosers, someone who picks freely is by implication not a beggar.

clue.text: Truth found by a 27 team, deserving fellows

parts.note: 27 is CRICKET, and a cricket team is an eleven, written XI in Roman numerals
the OM, Order of Merit, is an honour given to people of great distinction

explanation.surface: A truth discovered by a cricket side and some honoured men.
explanation.walkthrough: The 27 in the clue points to CRICKET, the theme answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a statement accepted as self-evidently true, a basic truth.

clue.text: Be unable to find what the railways did after Beeching

definitions.meaning: to fail to keep up with or find something

definitions.text: what the railways did after Beeching
definitions.meaning: the Beeching cuts of the 1960s closed thousands of miles of British railway line, so the railways literally parted with track

explanation.surface: Being unable to find something is likened to British railways after the 1960s cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Richard Beeching's 1963 report led to the closure of many British branch lines and their rails.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to fail to keep up with something, so being unable to find it.

clue.text: See 1
Testify against pained remark

parts.note: V is short for versus, against
ouch is what you say when hurt

explanation.surface: Someone gives evidence against a cry of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: To vouch is to testify or give personal assurance that something is true.

clue.text: Climbing fruit tree's endless song causes complaint

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing reads the letters upwards, so backwards
endless means the final letter of the tree is dropped

parts.note: citrus is a family of fruit trees
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: A climbing fruit tree's never-ending song brings on an ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Climbing' reads upwards; 'endless' trims the tree's last letter first. Urticaria is the medical name for nettle rash.
explanation.definitionFit: Urticaria is nettle rash, an itchy skin condition, so a medical complaint.

clue.text: Raw fruit in the underworld of atomic research

indicators.note: the reworked letters sit inside the underworld

parts.note: hell is the underworld

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Uncooked fruit lies in a hellish centre of nuclear science.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fruit' is an unusual anagram signal: the fruit of something is what it is made into. Harwell is in Oxfordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Harwell in Oxfordshire was home to Britain's Atomic Energy Research Establishment.

clue.text: Maid of Belmont resurrected as vamp

indicators.note: resurrected means raised up, so in a down clue the words read upwards

parts.note: a siren is a seductive woman, a vamp

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean maid comes back to life as a temptress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resurrected' turns AS SIREN upwards to NERIS SA. Belmont is Portia's home in The Merchant of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerissa is Portia's waiting-woman at Belmont in Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice.

clue.text: New members give bookmakers a new start

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is replaced with a different one

parts.note: bookies is the informal word for bookmakers

explanation.surface: Fresh recruits give the betting shops a fresh beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a new start' swaps the first letter B of BOOKIES for R.
explanation.definitionFit: Rookies are newcomers or recruits, new members of a team or force.

clue.text: Absolute monarch? I say!

parts.note: utter means absolute, complete
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A ruler with total power exclaims in surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is read literally: someone who can say 'I say' is a sayer.
explanation.definitionFit: A speaker who declares 'I say' is by definition someone who speaks, one who voices words.

clue.text: See if fuse works between 26 and 15, say

definitions.meaning: to check whether a fuse for lighting works is to try a lucifer, a light
a full international game of cricket, such as England against Australia

explanation.surface: Checking a fuse leads to an England versus Australia fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 is ENGLAND and 15 AUSTRALIA, whose Test series contest the Ashes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Test is a full international cricket fixture, as between England and Australia.

clue.text: Revolutionary on board like this?

parts.note: Che Guevara is the classic crossword revolutionary
SS, steamship, is the vessel people are on board

explanation.surface: A rebel taking up position on a board, as a piece might.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the game too: it is played on a board, where pieces make bold moves.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is the board game whose pieces move across a chequered board.

clue.text: House for 11, say

definitions.meaning: the upper chamber of Parliament, the House of Peers
the London ground that hosts Test cricket, a venue for such a match

explanation.surface: A building suited for a team of eleven.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 is TEST MATCH. Lord's in north London is the headquarters of cricket and a Test venue.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord's is a London cricket ground, and the House of Lords is the upper chamber of Parliament.

clue.text: How a Turk's got lost on Thames-side

indicators.note: having lost the way, the letters wander into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the S counting because it stands for has

explanation.surface: A Turkish man asks how he came to be lost by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got lost' rearranges HOW A TURKS. Southwark is a London borough on the south bank of the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Southwark is a district on the south bank of the River Thames in London.

clue.text: One left in another country

indicators.note: the two letters go inside the other country

parts.note: Austria, a different country from the answer
A is one, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone stayed behind in a foreign land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A and L inside AUSTRIA, a nation whose name differs by just those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia is a country, and the clue is the story of its name.

clue.text: Sally embracing member, in which lots are involved

indicators.note: the sally wraps itself around the member

parts.note: a sally is a sudden sortie by troops
a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A sudden attack takes in a limb during a lottery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a woman's name but is a military sortie; 'embracing' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Sortilege is divination by drawing lots, so lots are central to it.

clue.text: Leading 27-er packs trunk with lead

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A top cricketer stuffs his luggage with lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packs' rearranges TRUNK and LEAD. 27 is CRICKET.
explanation.definitionFit: Sachin Tendulkar of India is one of the leading cricketers of all time.

clue.text: Deal with cars etc

definitions.meaning: to trade or do business, often illicitly

explanation.surface: An instruction to handle cars and similar vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic means trade as a verb and the vehicles on a road as a noun.

clue.text: Capital at hand for comedian George, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the words are spoken out loud

parts.note: near is at hand, and George Robey was an English music-hall comedian

explanation.surface: A city is close to a famous comedian, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: George Robey was a celebrated British music-hall comic of the early 20th century.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya.

clue.text: Fool keeps fellow disputed by 26 and 15

indicators.note: the fool keeps the fellow inside

parts.note: an ass is a fool
he stands for a male person, a fellow

explanation.surface: An idiot holds on to a man that two countries argue over.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 is ENGLAND and 15 AUSTRALIA, who play cricket for the Ashes, a small urn.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ashes is the Test cricket series contested between England and Australia.

clue.text: Tool for boring holes in part of foot, reportedly a panacea

parts.note: an awl bores holes, and the heel is part of the foot, giving heel awl

explanation.surface: A cobbler's tool used in a heel is said to be a cure for all ills.
explanation.definitionFit: A heal-all is a remedy for everything, which is what panacea means.

clue.text: Be valid as comedian

definitions.meaning: an argument that holds good under scrutiny
a comic who performs solo before an audience

explanation.surface: Being sound like a comic.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand up is to hold good, and a stand-up is a solo comic.

clue.text: An expression of contempt that is copied

parts.note: pish is an exclamation of scorn

explanation.surface: A scornful exclamation, that is, one that was imitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' is a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Apish means imitative like an ape, so given to copying others, or copied.

clue.text: Leading 27-er, man with a life and Zhivago's girl

parts.note: Monty Python's film is Life of Brian
Lara is the heroine loved by Doctor Zhivago

explanation.surface: A top cricketer is a man with a past and a novel's heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 is CRICKET. 'a life' points to the Monty Python film Life of Brian.
explanation.definitionFit: Brian Lara of the West Indies is one of cricket's greatest batsmen.

clue.text: Stay for a time in the bathroom

parts.note: bide means stay or wait

explanation.surface: Lingering for a while in the washroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A bidet is a low washing basin found in a bathroom.

the Roman numeral for one is I

clue.text: Nut and (etymologically) acorn country
